title: Repair scope-based cleanup
prompt: Track how many LiveToken objects exist. Construction adds one; destruction removes one. Copying is disabled, so each token has exactly one end. Single-threaded use only.
signature: class LiveToken: inline static int live; constructor; destructor; deleted copy
starter:
#include <iostream>

class LiveToken{public:inline static int live=0;LiveToken(){++live;}~LiveToken(){}LiveToken(const LiveToken&)=delete;LiveToken& operator=(const LiveToken&)=delete;};
solution:
#include <iostream>

class LiveToken{public:inline static int live=0;LiveToken(){++live;}~LiveToken(){--live;}LiveToken(const LiveToken&)=delete;LiveToken& operator=(const LiveToken&)=delete;};

tests.label: One live in scope
tests.hint: Construction increases count while the object exists.

tests.label: After first scope
tests.hint: Destruction at the closing brace must decrease count.

tests.label: After second scope
tests.hint: Both destructors run after leaving scope.

hints: A destructor runs automatically at the end of an object’s lifetime.
Decrement the shared count exactly once in the destructor.
explanation: The live count is a teaching model for lifetime. The object owns one count contribution until destruction, including during exception unwinding.
